content.user_title: Improve Code Reviews With Structured Feedback
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss important risks or become hard to act on. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review method with clear severity, rationale, and follow-up questions.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews through context gathering, high-level review, line-by-line checks, and summary decisions.
Provides severity labels for blocking issues, important concerns, nits, suggestions, learning notes, and praise.
Includes checklists for security, performance, testing, authentication, authorization, input validation, and data protection.
Offers language-specific review patterns for Python and TypeScript or JavaScript examples.
Supports architecture review, staged review planning, and review disagreement handling.
limitations: It provides review guidance and does not automatically inspect a repository without user-provided code or diffs.
It does not replace project-specific standards, threat models, or human ownership decisions.
It cannot prove runtime behavior without tests, logs, or execution results.
It is focused on reviewing changes, not implementing fixes.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests Consistently
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable review process that separates blocking issues from suggestions and nits.

use_cases.title: Coach Reviewers on Better Feedback
use_cases.description: Teach reviewers to write specific, respectful comments with severity and clear next steps.

use_cases.title: Create Team Review Standards
use_cases.description: Build shared checklists for correctness, security, performance, testing, and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request diff. Group findings by blocking, important, and minor. Include rationale and test coverage notes.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a change with user input or sensitive data
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets, data exposure, and common vulnerabilities. Cite the exact risky behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Mentoring Feedback Rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite these review comments to be specific, actionable, and respectful. Preserve technical concerns and add severity labels.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Review Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a large feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this feature design and diff. Identify architectural risks, review stages, alternatives, test strategy, and unresolved questions.

output_examples.input: A pull request changes payment calculation and adds limited tests.
output: Blocking: clarify rounding behavior for tax and discounts before merge.
Important: add tests for zero-value orders, multiple discounts, and currency boundaries.
Minor: rename unclear variables where the domain meaning is hidden.

output_examples.input: A reviewer wrote harsh comments on a junior developer pull request.
output: Rewritten feedback focuses on the code behavior, explains the risk, and suggests one concrete fix.
The response separates required changes from learning notes and optional style suggestions.

output_examples.input: A large feature changes APIs, storage, and background jobs.
output: Recommended review split: interfaces first, implementation second, integration and tests third.
Open questions cover scaling, rollback, observability, and compatibility with existing patterns.

best_practices: Provide the pull request description, linked issue, diff, tests, and known constraints before asking for review.
Ask for severity-grouped findings so authors can separate required fixes from optional suggestions.
Use the security and performance checklists when the change handles input, secrets, data, or hot paths.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad approval without sharing the actual code or behavioral requirements.
Do not treat style preferences as blocking issues when automated tools or team standards should decide them.
Do not use the skill to implement fixes when the task requires an independent review.

faq.question: What does this skill help review?
faq.answer: It helps review pull requests, code changes, review standards, and mentoring feedback.

faq.question: Does it run tests or inspect repositories automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reviews the code, diff, context, and test results that the user provides.

faq.question: Can it review security risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checklists for authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets, data protection, and common vulnerabilities.

faq.question: Can it help write better review comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn vague or harsh feedback into specific, actionable, and respectful comments.

faq.question: Is it useful for architecture reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports staged review planning, design questions, alternatives, and tradeoff discussion.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
